summary: The MCO-for-WMT swap lowers the 10% stress loss from -$23.42 to about -$22.05 and leaves every name under the 15% cap. It also concentrates the book further: Staples rises to about 18.6% by bucket, WMT becomes the third-largest holding (about 10.4%), and the largest risk is unchanged by either trade, since VOO and VTI (23.6% of equity) sit 0.06% above one shared SPY 200-day stop. No lesson in learning.json names the Implicator in applies_to, and there are no Implicator graded_calls yet. L3's caveat that the bucket should be checked against the business shaped how I read MCO: I treat it as financial data with MSCI, not as Industrials.

checks.concentration: Sells MCO in full, about $23.63 at the 481.29 mark (3.81% of $620.35 equity). Packet bucket: Industrials falls from 8.86% to 5.05%, leaving FAST as the only name. By business (L3), the financial-data sleeve shrinks from about 8.06% (MCO+MSCI) to 4.25% (MSCI alone). Cash rises to about $94.65 before P2. The asset mix is unchanged in kind: stocks fall from about 64.9% to 61.1% of equity before P2, equity ETFs stay at 23.6%, and there are no bond, gold or crypto positions. BND, IEF and VNQ are buy-blocked by wash-sale windows, so the book has no non-equity diversifier.
checks.overlap: Removes overlap rather than adding it. MCO and MSCI fail leverage_not_up together and fell about 4.3%/4.2% together on 11-17, so cutting one halves that shared risk. Both are small constituents of VOO/VTI, so the look-through exposure there remains, but it is immaterial.
checks.tax: There is one lot: 0.049092 sh at $509.04, opened 2026-11-16 (3 days held) and long-term on 2027-11-17, so FIFO takes it all. The loss is short-term, about -$1.36 at the mark (-5.45%). With a year to go there is no long-term timing to protect, and the realized loss is small.
checks.wash_sale: none. The only MCO purchase in the last 30 days is the 11-16 lot being sold in full, so no other shares remain to absorb the loss. Consequence: MCO becomes buy-blocked through about 2026-12-19. Do not plan a re-entry if the invalidation (close back above $509.04) fires inside that window, or the loss will be disallowed. MSCI and VOO/VTI are not substantially identical.
checks.summary: Clean exit: a small short-term loss with no lot-timing cost, and it cuts the stress loss by about $1.28. It reduces the avoided-bucket and rising-leverage financial-data overlap. Watch the 30-day re-buy block.

checks.concentration: WMT goes from $49.43 (7.97%) to about $64.43 (about 10.39%), under the 15% cap and within the $43.34 buy cap. It becomes the third-largest holding after VOO (13.5%) and DPZ (11.57%), just ahead of VTI (10.14%). The Staples bucket rises from 16.15% to about 18.57% (WMT 10.39%, KR 5.73%, SAM 2.45%). By SIC label, adding DPZ (11.57%, a wholesale-groceries mislabel per L3) puts the 'staples' stack near 30%, though DPZ's bucket is Consumer Discretionary. With P1, cash ends at about $79.65 (12.84%), invested about 87.2%. Stock share is about 63.5% of equity and US broad-equity ETFs stay at 23.6%.
checks.overlap: Adds directly to the portfolio's largest sector lean. WMT, KR and SAM are one Staples factor bet: they fell together on 11-03 and 11-06 per L3. The beta-based stress shows Staples as a cushion (WMT +0.58, KR +6.08, SAM +2.86 per $100), and that understates this shared factor risk. KR and SAM's negative betas are flagged as artifacts in their own theses. WMT is also a large constituent of VOO/VTI, so there is a small look-through overlap. The add does not join the shared VOO/VTI SPY stop (L9): WMT has its own stop.
checks.tax: Buy: it creates a new short-term lot. Later sells go FIFO, so the 2026-10-20 lot at $118.378 (long-term on 2027-10-21, about +7.6% at the mark) would go first. At a fill near the 127.36 mark the blended cost becomes about $120.43 (about 0.514 sh). The whole-position stop at $119.00 then sits only about 1.2% under blended cost and about 6.6% under the new lot. The PM should restate the stop text from the blended cost after the fill (L6). A post-print gap up would widen the new lot's distance to the stop.
checks.wash_sale: none. The only recent WMT realization (2026-11-13 trim) was a gain of +$1.80, and WMT is not in buy_blocked.
checks.summary: It fits under the caps and barely moves the stress number (+$0.09 by beta). In practice it raises Staples to about 18.6% and makes WMT a 10%+ position bought on print day, so the real risk is a correlated Staples drawdown and post-print chasing, not market beta.

notes: Stress arithmetic uses the packet's per-$100 figures only. P1 removes $23.63 x -5.43/100 = -$1.283, so the loss shrinks by $1.283. P2 adds $15 x +0.58/100 = +$0.087. Result: -23.42 + 1.283 + 0.087 = -22.05. VOO and VTI alone contribute about -$14.66 of the -$22.05. Neither proposal touches the main concentration: 23.6% of equity rides on one SPY 200-day line 0.06% away. If it trips and both are sold, cash would go to about 36%, with no bond or gold sleeve available until the BND (about 12-16) and IEF/VNQ (about 12-13) wash windows clear. Crypto: none held and none proposed, so the 5% cap and the 365-day vol check do not apply.
